newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Lagging Belgian shares to catch up in near term.
newsitem.headline: Lagging Belgian shares to catch up in near term.

text.p: Belgian shares are seen climbing higher in the next few days as they catch up with neighbouring markets, analysts said on Tuesday.
"We've been lagging the German and Dutch markets over the last couple of weeks and still have some way to go to catch up," said an analyst. "The market is relatively cheap."
The Bel-20 index closed up 13.6 points or 0.77 percent at 1,788.38 points as a healthy 2.3 billion francs worth of Belgian shares changed hands.
"The Dow, the dollar and bonds are strong. Everything is in place for our market to rise," said the analyst.

Steel wire maker Bekaert was the biggest gainer, climbing a solid 2.7 percent to 24,775 francs. Retailer Delhaize was also in demand, rising two percent to 1,785 francs with more than 64,000 shares traded.
Both were lifted by the stronger dollar.

Retailer GIB finished four francs up at 1,312 francs after early gains took it 0.9 percent higher to 1,320 francs. A GIB spokesman described as "premature" an earlier Belgian newspaper report that the company was close to selling its Sarma textiles stores chain.
